solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Film's starting point abroad

definitions.note: the definition plus 's, read as 'Film is'

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered or astray, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cinema buff remarks that a movie's opening was filmed overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' signals rearranging the thirteen letters of STARTING POINT. 'Film's' reads as 'Film is', so the definition leads straight into the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainspotting is the 1996 Danny Boyle movie adapted from Irvine Welsh's novel about Edinburgh addicts.

clue.text: Flog junk round hotel

indicators.note: round says the word for junk is placed around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: junk means trash, rubbish
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone tries to sell off rubbish lying around a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' looks like British slang for sell, but here it means beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog someone is to beat them with a whip or stick, a synonym of thrash.

clue.text: Suddenly, everyone agreed about carbon

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: about says the phrase for agreed goes around the next piece

parts.note: to be at one is to be in agreement
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A meeting where, without warning, everybody concurred on carbon emissions.
explanation.walkthrough: AT ONE is split to take C, giving AT ONC E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening all at once happens abruptly, without warning, the same idea as suddenly.

clue.text: Beginning or ending of mountain climb

indicators.note: ending of points to the final letter of the next word only

parts.note: a climb is an ascent

explanation.surface: A mountaineer wonders whether this is the start or the finish of the ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning or ending' looks like a choice between two letters; 'Beginning' is the definition and 'or' just links it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into being, an adjective for something at its beginning.

clue.text: Government leader to prepare member of the clergy

parts.note: to prime something is to prepare it, as with paint or a pump
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: The head of government gets a churchman ready.
explanation.definitionFit: The prime minister heads the government in Britain and many other parliamentary systems.

clue.text: Awkward drunk

definitions.meaning: a ... situation is a difficult, awkward one

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy is clumsy and embarrassing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight covers both a tricky spot, as in a tight corner, and being intoxicated.

clue.text: What Arctic explorer covers?

indicators.note: covers says the answer is concealed within the words Arctic explorer

explanation.surface: A quiz question about what a polar traveller crosses.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the join of 'ArctIC Explorer', and the whole clue also defines it: frozen sea is what such an explorer traverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar explorers trek across frozen sea and glaciers, so frozen water is what they cover.

clue.text: Turn on charm, mostly to get the honest truth

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

indicators.note: mostly means the word for charm loses its final letter

parts.note: a charm is a spell

explanation.surface: Advice to be charming in order to extract a frank confession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn on charm' reads as one phrase; it is GO, 'on' joining it to SPEL(L).
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel truth, or simply gospel, means something wholly reliable and true.

clue.text: Parts reportedly for luxury car

indicators.note: reportedly says we want a word sounding like the one for parts

parts.note: actors' parts are roles

explanation.surface: Supposedly spare parts for an expensive motor.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolls is the short name for a Rolls-Royce, the British marque of luxury cars.

clue.text: Entrance made by different singers

indicators.note: different suggests the letters of singers made into something other

explanation.surface: A grand entry staged by a variety of vocalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a formal word for going in or a means of entering.

clue.text: Defiant words, likewise, at that place

parts.note: so means likewise, as in 'so do I'
there means at that place

explanation.surface: Someone defiantly says the same, pointing over yonder.
explanation.definitionFit: 'So there!' is a childish retort said to assert oneself in defiance.

clue.text: Redesigned seat fitted with wide strap

indicators.note: fitted with says the rearranged seat has the letter placed inside it
redesigned means the letters of seat are given a new layout

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for wide

explanation.surface: A car seat remodelled and given a broad belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redesigned' rearranges SEAT to TASE, and 'fitted with' puts W inside. A tawse is a Scottish leather strap once used to punish schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: A tawse is a leather strap with split tails, formerly used in Scottish schools for corporal punishment.

clue.text: Justified, conflict with editor following angry tirade

indicators.note: following says the editor comes after the tirade

parts.note: war is armed conflict
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: An editor defends a war after a furious outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Warranted means having good grounds, a synonym of justified.

clue.text: Pound split by Italian page for fussy fault-finder

indicators.note: split by says the word for pound is broken open to take the other pieces

parts.note: nicker is British slang for a pound sterling
IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A fussy critic beats up an Italian and a pageboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like a verb; it is NICKER, British slang for one pound sterling, split after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitpicker obsesses over trivial errors, so the phrase describes a pedantic critic.

clue.text: Expertise of king who won unexpectedly

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of who won fall out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A monarch's skill brought him a surprise victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges WHO WON into NOWHOW, after K.
explanation.definitionFit: Know-how is practical skill or technical knowledge, another word for expertise.

clue.text: Armed guard in foreign sector

indicators.note: foreign suggests the letters of sector are made strange, shaken up

explanation.surface: Soldiers protecting a convoy in an overseas zone.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a body of guards accompanying someone for protection.

clue.text: Loud roar coming from fifty entering underneath

indicators.note: entering says the numeral goes into the word for underneath

parts.note: below means underneath
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A deep roar rising from fifty people coming in below.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellow is a deep, loud shout, a near synonym of roar.

clue.text: Box containing eastern throwing weapon

indicators.note: containing says the word for box holds the letter inside it

parts.note: to box in practice is to spar

explanation.surface: A crate holding an Oriental javelin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a noun, a container; it is the verb, to spar.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long pole weapon that can be hurled, like a javelin.

clue.text: Cap removed from toy firearm

indicators.note: cap is the top letter of a down entry, so removing it drops the first letter

parts.note: a trifle is a toy, a thing of little value

explanation.surface: A toy gun has lost its cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' suggests the toy gun's caps; it means the first letter of TRIFLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled gun fired from the shoulder.

clue.text: Very behindhand after electric current cut off

indicators.note: after places the phrase for very behindhand behind the symbol for current

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics
so means very
behindhand means late

explanation.surface: Someone running very late after a power cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate means to separate or keep apart, as in being cut off from others.

clue.text: Rejected set of clothes Oscar collected

indicators.note: collected says the word for set of clothes gathers up the letter inside it

parts.note: an outfit is a set of clothes
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Oscar picked up a cast-off suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award; it is the code word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel out of it is to feel excluded, left out by a group.

clue.text: Part of body shown in photo, enlarged

indicators.note: shown in says the answer is displayed inside the words photo enlarged

explanation.surface: A body part visible in a blown-up picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe is one of the digits of the foot, a part of the body.

clue.text: Very warm, the Spanish inn

parts.note: very warm means hot
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A sweltering Spanish guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a place offering lodging to travellers, as a hotel does.

clue.text: Operetta article somehow worried my wife

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of worried my are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: A man frets that an item in the paper has upset his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator rearranges WORRIED MY into MERRYWIDO, with W added.
explanation.definitionFit: The Merry Widow is Franz Lehár's 1905 Viennese operetta.
